_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: चित्तैकाग्र्योपयोगिनीं देहादिधारणां दर्शयन्नाह सममिति द्वाभ्याम्
showing bodily posture and the like useful for one-pointedness of mind, he speaks in two verses beginning ‘straight’
काय इति देहमध्यभागो विवक्षितः
‘body’ means the middle portion of the body
कायश्च शिरश्च ग्रीवा च कायशिरोग्रीवं मूलाधारादारभ्य मूर्धाग्रपर्यन्तं सममवक्रं निश्चलं धारयन् स्थिरः
holding body, head, and neck—from the base to the crown—straight, unbent, unmoving, he should remain steady
दृढप्रयत्नो भूत्वेत्यर्थः
that is, making firm effort
स्वकीयं नासिकाग्रं संप्रेक्ष्य च अर्धनिमीलितनेत्र इत्यर्थः
gazing at the tip of his own nose means with eyes half closed
इतस्ततो दिशश्चानवलोकयन्नासीतेत्युत्तरेणान्वयः
it connects with the next verse: he should sit without looking around in different directions
प्रशान्तेति
with ‘tranquil’
प्रशान्त आत्मा चित्तं यस्य
one whose self, mind, is tranquil
विगता भीर्भयं यस्य
whose fear has departed
ब्रह्मचारिव्रते ब्रह्मचर्ये स्थितः सन्
remaining established in the vow of celibacy
मनः संयम्य प्रत्याहृत्य
restraining and withdrawing the mind
मय्येव चित्तं यस्य अहमेव परः पुरुषार्थो यस्य स मत्परः
one whose mind is in Me alone and for whom I alone am the supreme human goal is ‘devoted to Me’
एवं युक्तो भूत्वा आसीत तिष्ठेत्
becoming disciplined in this way, he should sit, remain
योगाभ्यासफलमाह युञ्जन्नेवमिति
he states the fruit of yoga practice with ‘practicing thus’
एवमुक्तप्रकारेण सदात्मानं मनो युञ्जन् समाहितं कुर्वन्
constantly yoking the self, the mind, making it composed in the stated manner
नियतं निरुद्धं मानसं चित्तं यस्य सः
one whose mental activity, mind, is controlled and restrained
शान्तिं संसारोपरतिं प्राप्नोति
attains peace, cessation of saṃsāra
कथंभूताम् निर्वाणं परमं प्राप्यं यस्यां तां मत्संस्थां मद्रूपेणावस्थितिम्
what kind? the peace whose supreme attainment is nirvāṇa, abiding in Me, remaining in My nature
योगाभ्यासनिष्ठस्याहारादिनियममाह नेति द्वाभ्याम्
he gives the rules concerning food and the like for one established in yoga practice in two verses beginning ‘not’
अत्यन्तमधिकं भुञ्जानस्य एकान्तमत्यन्तमभुञ्जानस्यापि योगः समाधिर्न भवति
samādhi does not arise for one who eats excessively, nor for one who does not eat at all
तथातिनिद्राशीलस्यातिजाग्रतश्च योगो नैवास्ति
likewise yoga does not exist for one given to excessive sleep or excessive wakefulness
तर्हि कथंभूतस्य योगो भवतीत्यत आह युक्तेति
then for what kind of person does yoga arise? he says ‘regulated’
युक्तो नियत आहारो विहारश्च गतिर्यस्य
one whose food and recreation, movement, are regulated
कर्मसु कार्येषु युक्ता नियतैव चेष्टा यस्य
whose activity in duties is regulated
युक्तौ नियतौ स्वप्नावबोधौ निद्राजागरौ यस्य
whose sleep and waking are regulated
तस्य दुःखनिवर्तको योगो भवति सिध्यति
for him yoga that removes suffering arises and succeeds
कदा निष्पन्नयोगः पुरुषो भवतीत्यपेक्षायामाह यदेति
when does a person become perfected in yoga? he says ‘when’
विनियतं विशेषेण निरुद्धं सच्चित्तमात्मन्येव यदा निश्चलं तिष्ठति
when his thoroughly restrained mind remains motionless in the Self alone
किंच सर्वकामेभ्य ऐहिकामुष्मिकभोगेभ्यो विगततृष्णो भवति
and when thirst has departed for all desires, enjoyments here and hereafter
तदा प्राप्तयोग इत्युच्यते
then he is said to have attained yoga
आत्मैकाकारतयावस्थितस्य चित्तस्योपमानमाह यथेति
he gives an illustration for the mind abiding in the single form of the Self with ‘as’
वातशून्ये देशे स्थितो दीपो यथा नेङ्गते न विचलति सा उपमा दृष्टान्तः
a lamp standing in a windless place does not flicker or move; that is the illustration
कस्य आत्मविषयं योगं युञ्जतोऽभ्यसतो योगिनो यतं नियतं चित्तं यस्य
for the restrained, controlled mind of the yogin practicing yoga concerning the Self
निष्कम्पतया प्रकाशकतया च दीपवत्तिष्ठतीत्यर्थः
it remains like a lamp because it is unmoving and illuminating; this is the meaning
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डवेत्यादौ कर्मैव योगशब्देनोक्तम्
in ‘what they call renunciation, know that as yoga, O Pāṇḍava,’ action itself was denoted by the word yoga
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्तीत्यादौ तु समाधिर्योगशब्देनोक्तः
but in ‘yoga does not belong to one who eats excessively,’ samādhi is denoted by yoga
तत्र मुख्यो योगः क इत्यपेक्षायां समाधिमेव स्वरूपतः फलतश्च लक्षयन् स एव मुख्यो योग इत्याह यत्रेति सार्धैस्त्रिभिः
when asked which is yoga in the primary sense, he defines samādhi by its nature and fruit and says it alone is primary yoga in three and a half verses beginning ‘where’
यत्र यस्मिन्नवस्थाविशेषे योगाभ्यासेन निरुद्धं चित्तमुपरतं भवतीति योगस्य स्वरूपलक्षणमुक्तम्
the definition of yoga’s nature is: the state in which the mind restrained through yoga practice comes to rest
तथाच पातञ्जलं सूत्रम् योगश्चित्तवृत्तिनिरोधः इति
thus Patañjali’s aphorism says ‘yoga is restraint of the modifications of mind’
इष्टप्राप्तिलक्षणेन फलेन तमेव लक्षयति
he also defines it by the fruit characterized by attainment of what is desired
यत्र च यस्मिन्नवस्थाविशेषे आत्मना शुद्धेन मनसात्मानमेव पश्यति नतु देहादि
in that state, by the purified self, mind, one sees the Self alone and not body and the like
पश्यंश्चात्मन्येव तुष्यति नतु विषयेषु
seeing it, one is satisfied in the Self alone, not in objects
यत्रेत्यादीनां यच्छब्दानां तं योगसंज्ञितं विद्यादिति चतुर्थेनान्वयः
the relative pronouns beginning ‘where’ connect with the fourth verse: ‘know that as what is called yoga’
आत्मन्येव तोषे हेतुमाह सुखमिति
he states the reason for satisfaction in the Self alone with ‘happiness’
यत्र यस्मिन्नवस्थाविशेषे यत्तत्किमपि निरतिशयमात्यन्तिकं नित्यं सुखं वेत्ति
in that state one knows some unsurpassed, absolute, eternal happiness
ननु तदा विषयेन्द्रियसंबन्धाभावात्कुतः सुखं स्यात्तत्राह अतीन्द्रियं विषयेन्द्रियसंबन्धातीतम्
objection: without connection between senses and objects, whence happiness? he says it is beyond the senses, beyond relation between objects and senses
केवलं बुद्ध्यैवात्माकारतया ग्राह्यम्
grasped only by the intellect when it takes the form of the Self
अतएव च यत्र स्थितः संस्तत्त्वत आत्मस्वरूपान्नैव चलति
therefore, established there, one does not move from the true nature of the Self
अचलत्वमेवोपपादयति यमिति
he establishes that immovability with ‘which’
यमात्मसुखरूपलाभं लब्ध्वा ततोऽधिकमपरं लाभं न मन्यते न चिन्तयति तस्यैव निरतिशयसुखत्वात्
having attained the gain consisting of happiness of the Self, one does not regard or think of another gain as greater, because that alone is unsurpassed happiness
यस्मिंश्च स्थितो महतापि शीतोष्णादिदुःखेन न विचाल्यते नाभिभूयते
established in it, one is not shaken or overcome even by great suffering such as heat and cold
एतेनेष्टनिवृत्तिफलेनापि योगलक्षणमुक्तं द्रष्टव्यम्
by this fruit consisting in removal of the undesirable, a definition of yoga too should be understood
य एवंभूतोऽवस्थाविशेषस्तमाह तमित्यर्धेन
he states the state of this kind in half a verse with ‘that’
दुःखशब्देन दुःखमिश्रितत्वाद्वैषयिकं सुखमपि गृह्यते
by the word suffering, sensory pleasure too is included because it is mixed with suffering
दुःखस्य संयोगेन स्पर्शमात्रेणापि वियोगो यस्मिंस्तमवस्थाविशेषं योगसंज्ञितं योगशब्दवाच्यं जानीयात्
know as ‘yoga’ that special state in which there is separation even from mere contact with the conjunction of suffering
परमात्मना क्षेत्रज्ञस्य योजनं योगः
yoga is joining of the knower of the field with the Supreme Self
यद्वा दुःखसंयोगेन वियोग एव शूरे कातरशब्दवद्विरुद्धलक्षणया योग उच्यते
or separation from conjunction with suffering is called yoga by an opposite indication, like calling a hero ‘coward’ ironically
कर्मणि तु योगशब्दस्तदुपायत्वादौपचारिक एवेति भावः
in relation to action, the word yoga is secondary because action is a means to it; this is the intention
यस्मादेवं महाफलो योगस्तस्मात्स एव यत्नतोऽभ्यसनीय इत्याह स इति सार्धेन
because yoga has such a great fruit, it must be practiced with effort; he says this in a verse and a half beginning ‘that’
स यो निश्चयेन शास्त्राचार्योपदेशजनितेन योक्तव्योऽभ्यसनीयः
it should be practiced with determination born from instruction of scripture and teacher
यद्यपि शीघ्रं न सिध्यति तथाप्यनिर्विण्णेन निर्वेदरहितेन चेतसा योक्तव्यः
even if it does not succeed quickly, it should be practiced with a mind free from discouragement
दुःखबुद्ध्या प्रयत्नशैथिल्यं निर्वेदः
discouragement means slackening of effort through the thought that it is painful
किंच संकल्पेति
and further, with ‘desires born of conception’
संकल्पात्प्रभवो येषां तान्योगप्रतिकूलान्सर्वान्कामानशेषतः सवासनांस्त्यक्त्वा
abandoning without remainder, together with their latent impressions, all desires born from conception and opposed to yoga
मनसैव विषयदोषदर्शिना सर्वतः प्रसरन्तमिन्द्रियसमूहं विशेषेण नियम्य
with the mind itself seeing defects in objects, thoroughly restraining the group of senses that spreads in all directions
योगो योक्तव्य इति पूर्वेणान्वयः
yoga should be practiced; this connects with the preceding statement
